title: Console observability slimline: feature-fencing matrix and go/no-go criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: reduce initial Console observability surface to a defensible MVP while preserving critical user journeys for incident triage and cost attribution. This ticket captures the scope cuts, a fencing matrix that maps features to user personas, and explicit go/no-go acceptance criteria for launch. Background: earlier PRD requested a broad set of cards (route heatmaps, full trace waterfall, per-token cost breakdown, anomaly detection). Constraint: telemetry ingestion and storage budget limits require removing or deferring high-cardinality surfaces. Goal: deliver a compact set of dashboards and trace controls that let SREs and platform engineers answer top-3 operational questions (is system healthy, which routes are expensive, which deploy caused regression) within latency and cost SLOs.
decisions: Cut: Defer anomaly-detection ML scoring (high ingestion/compute) — surface placeholder and link to future roadmap
Cut: Remove per-tenant token-by-token replay UI from MVP; keep sampled token-level inspector accessible via deep link
Keep: Route-level cost summary card (top 25 routes by spend) with 7d spike detection
Keep: Mini trace explorer limited to 1k-span samples and configurable retention window for console queries
Replace: Full waterfall traces with condensed span timeline and top-error highlighting to reduce rendering and API load
scope_changes: Original scope included 10 dashboard cards; MVP scope trimmed to 4 cards: Health Summary, Route Cost Summary, Recent Errors, Mini Trace Explorer
Tracing: limit trace detail to 1k-span sampling and cap simultaneous query window to 1 minute of data
Cost breakdown: aggregate token cost to route-level buckets instead of per-request line items for MVP
Telemetry retention: reduce default console retention sampling to 1% for debug-level events; critical events remain 100%
acceptance_criteria: Health Summary: displays service-level success rate and p95 latency for top routes; refreshes within 15s of ingest
Route Cost Summary: shows top 25 routes by spend, delta vs prior 7d, and links to raw sample traces
Mini Trace Explorer: returns sampled traces within 3s for queries spanning up to 1 minute; UI shows condensed timeline and top-3 error spans
Rendering & Cost SLOs: console telemetry ingest + query load for MVP surface must not increase monthly telemetry bill > 12% relative to baseline
Graceful degradation: when trace backend overloads, UI surfaces a deterministic fallback message and offers a one-click retry to cheaper aggregated view
E2E tests: synthetic scenarios covering cost spike, increased error rate, and degraded downstream model return expected console flagged alerts
Security & Audit: all console queries are logged to audit pipeline; no sensitive prompt payloads are exposed in UI by default
risks: Reduced fidelity may frustrate early adopters who expect full waterfall traces; risk mitigated by clear messaging and a migration path
Sampling defaults might mask intermittent regressions — mitigation: add a toggle for higher sampling in customer-specific dedicated deployments
Performance: condensed timelines still require efficient rendering; engineering dependency on ENG-67212 for front-end virtualization is blocking
Billing: incorrect aggregation could undercount costs; require cross-check with billing team before launch
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): enable MVP surface for internal Redwood teams and 3 pilot customers for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (Opt-in Beta): enable for customers on request with monitoring of telemetry bill and UX feedback
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with communications, migration guide, and documented upgrade path to full surface
Rollback criteria: >20% telemetry cost increase or >10% increase in frontend error rate in canary -> roll back to aggregated-only view
